text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear position against self-driving cars","quality":"stance clarity","description":"The essay states a definite argument and keeps its opposition to driverless cars easy to identify throughout."},{"evidence":"repeated rhetorical questions and warnings","quality":"persuasive voice","description":"It uses a more forceful, argumentative tone that actively tries to persuade the reader rather than just describe the topic."},{"evidence":"money, roads, safety, liability points in separate paragraphs","quality":"argument development","description":"The essay develops multiple reasons against driverless cars instead of relying on only one main concern."},{"evidence":"mentions expense, safety, government road changes, and blame in accidents","quality":"use of source-based reasoning","description":"It draws on several article details to build its case and connect them to its own position."},{"evidence":"closing question about whether a 'safe car' will really be safer","quality":"conclusionary impact","description":"The ending leaves the reader with a final challenge that reinforces the argument instead of ending abruptly."}]}
